transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-12
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (AE), Priya (SE), Marco (CSM) — Chris (Aventra), Leah (PM), Samir (Data Eng), Nora (Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on recent accuracy delta observed on the clinical triage prompt set. Reviewed failing examples, potential root causes (prompt drift, tokenization mismatch, quantization artefacts), and a rollback/playbook for canary -> stable model transitions. Agreed on data handoff, stability run, and a rollback drill next week.

Topics covered:
- Recent regression signals and scorecard deltas
- Prompt set curation and hidden label inconsistencies
- Guardrail false positives vs false negatives tradeoffs
- Rollback and canary promotion playbook
- Security note on logs/KMS access for debug runs

Action items (quick): Priya to run detailed latency/cost on failing set; Chris to upload 300 failing prompts; Jordan to share Dedicated pricing; schedule rollback drill.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan (AE): all right hi everyone uh thanks for joining on time, we got a short agenda, uh quick sync on the accuracy delta you flagged and then walk through rollback steps.
00:14 Chris (Aventra): yeah thanks Jordan. We saw a bump in false positives on the triage set, roughly from 4.2% to about 7.8% after the latest canary. It's not across the board but concentrated on certain prompt templates.
00:29 Priya (SE): okay can you share an example, is this the symptom where the model hallucinates an allergy where there is none?
00:36 Chris: yeah exactly, like prompts that mention \"patient reports hives\" sometimes the model overcalls \"anaphylaxis\" even when vitals are normal, which our ruleset should block.
00:48 Leah (PM): to add, a couple of those prompts came from the new intake flow we launched two weeks ago, there might be phrasing differences.
00:58 Samir (Data Eng): we dropped them into the eval harness, and the scorecard delta spiked primarily on the safety & severity labels.
01:10 Priya: got it. Two quick suspects: prompt phrasing drift and policy/guardrail threshold sensitivity. Also need to confirm tokenization differences if we switched quantized artifacts.
01:24 Jordan: and remind me, are we running the same model binary on canary as prod? I thought we had an optimized quantized variant for canary.
01:32 Marco (CSM): correct, canary is q4_0 micro-quant variant with a slightly different kernel chain, prod is q4_0 baseline.
01:40 Nora (Security): quick security question — if we run a debug/stability run, what logs will Redwood need and do we need to red-team anything? we have strict PHI constraints.
01:52 Jordan: good point. We'll limit logs to token-latency and model outputs hashed; no raw PHI will be persisted. We'll use customer KMS for key wrap if you prefer.
02:06 Chris: that would be required yes, any raw transcript needs to be redacted.
02:12 Priya: to structure the investigation, plan A: reproduce delta in Redwood harness with identical prompts and model variant; plan B: ablation by prompt template; plan C: rollback if we can't fix within SLO.
02:28 Leah: what's the expected time to rollback? we need a playbook to minimize blast radius.
02:33 Jordan: we've got a rollback playbook — can do canary -> stable revert within 15 minutes if traffic is routed correctly; full rollback across regions might take up to 60. but we want a drill first.
02:46 Samir: on reproducing — we noticed some tokenization mismatches where punctuation from the intake flow gets normalized differently, could that lead to different attention patterns?
02:58 Priya: yes that can change position embeddings alignment slightly, particularly with longer clinical notes. We'll test with both normalized and raw inputs.
03:10 Chris: also, curious if Redwood Optimize's suggestion to batch at 64 was applied — could batching change perf and maybe affect generation due to cache behavior?
03:22 Priya: batching shouldn't change generation semantics but if KV cache invalidation or prefix caching is mishandled in the canary path, it could. we'll check cache hits and sequence alignments.
03:36 Jordan: okay so concrete triage steps: Priya reproduces locally in harness with raw and normalized prompts; run token-level diff and prefix cache stats; Marco to coordinate stability run on canary for 24h; Chris to upload failing prompts + expected labels.
03:52 Leah: one more thing — scorecard thresholds are pretty aggressive, can we look at moving the severity cutoff slightly to avoid false positives?
04:02 Priya: yes but we need to balance false negatives. suggest a temporary threshold relaxation for canary traffic only while we triage.
04:12 Nora: from security side we need audit logs for any rollback and a signed authorization from Aventra infra owners before we cut traffic.
04:22 Jordan: understood — we'll add a step to the playbook for signed roll approval and log capture.
04:30 Samir: when you run the harness, please surface the top 20 tokens that differ between prod and canary outputs for the failing prompts, that helps our labeling team.
04:43 Priya: yes we'll include that. Also will include latency and per-token cost run so you can see economic impact if we roll back to baseline.
04:54 Chris: timeline — if you can run the stability run tonight and we upload prompts by tomorrow EOD, can we aim for rollback drill Wednesday evening?
05:05 Jordan: that works. We'll tentatively schedule the drill for 2026-08-18 02:00 UTC, but will confirm after the stability run.
05:15 Leah: one more ask — can Redwood provide a simple compare view (side-by-side generation excerpts) for the 100 highest-confidence mismatches so our clinical review can triage faster?
05:27 Priya: yes we'll export a CSV and a small HTML diff viewer link; we'll send a link in the follow-up.
05:36 Marco: i'll own the scheduling and make sure infra stakeholders are in the rollback drill.
05:42 Jordan: great. Any other questions or blockers?
05:46 Chris: just one — cost impact if we keep canary disabled and roll back; what's the hit to us financially for switching to Dedicated baseline?
05:55 Jordan: i'll send updated pricing for Dedicated baseline vs burst, and show token-unit delta in the follow-up.
06:05 Nora: and we need confirmation that KMS keys will be used for debug runs and that no raw PHI leaves Aventra environment.
06:14 Jordan: confirmed, we'll use your KMS and only pull hashed outputs; we can also do ephemeral VPC access if needed for the 24h run.
06:25 Priya: all right i'll start the harness run now, expect initial artifacts by tomorrow.
06:30 Jordan: perfect, thanks everyone. recap: Priya runs token / cache diff and stability run; Chris uploads 300 failing prompts; Jordan sends pricing and scheduling; Marco schedules rollback drill. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
